title: Agilent 7890B Gas Chromatograph Operation Manual
locator: Chapter 4, Methods and Sequences, p. 38 onward. Chapter 6, chromatographic checkout, pp. 54–61, especially Table 4 for the FID.
summary: The manual explains what the instrument stores in a method and how to check the performance of the flame ionization detector. The checkout table separates inlet settings from column and detector conditions.
scope: Identify the inlet, detector, column and sampling hardware installed on the local GC. The checkout sample verifies instrument response under specified conditions. Food samples require their own method and calibration.
rights: Manufacturer link and original catalog summary.

title: Determination of fatty acid methyl esters by gas chromatography
locator: Scope and Principle. Part 1, preparation of methyl esters. Part 2, sections 3.1.1–3.1.3, inlet, oven and capillary column requirements.
summary: The Council describes preparing methyl esters from vegetable oils, separating them on a polar capillary column and measuring them by flame ionization. Its stated coverage is C12 to C24 fatty acid methyl esters, including specified cis and trans species.
scope: The preparation determines whether free fatty acids are included alongside bound fatty acids. Use a compatible capillary inlet and check separation of the isomers of interest before interpreting relative amounts.
rights: Council method link and original catalog summary.

title: Improving the Analysis of 37 Fatty Acid Methyl Esters
locator: Experimental, instrumentation. Table 1, standard mixture. Tables 2–5, configurations and conditions for each capillary column. Conclusions, isomer resolution.
summary: On a 7890B with FID, split/splitless inlet and 7683B liquid sampler, Agilent compared capillary columns using a 37-component FAME standard. The CP-Sil 88 column separated all components at baseline. The DB-FATWAX UI column had limited separation of the C18:1 cis/trans pair.
scope: This experiment addresses column selectivity using prepared standards. Check food-matrix recovery, derivatization and isomer resolution separately before adopting the method for an oil sample.
rights: Manufacturer application note link and original catalog summary.

title: Physical and Chemical Characterisation of Conventional and Nano/Emulsions: Influence of Vegetable Oils from Different Origins
version: Kampa et al., volume 11, article 681. DOI 10.3390/foods11050681
locator: Materials and methods, Oil Samples and section 2.4.1, Fatty Acid Composition. The preparation, GC configuration and peak-area calculation are specified there.
summary: The authors analyzed fatty acid methyl esters from olive, rapeseed and sunflower oils on a 7890B with an HP-5 column, split injection and FID. They averaged normalized peak areas from three injections to report relative composition.
scope: The comparison concerns five selected oil products and the reported peak-area fractions. An HP-5 separation of these fatty acids does not establish resolution of all positional or cis/trans isomers.
rights: Publisher open-access article link and original catalog summary.

title: Determination of Ethanol in Kombucha Products: Single-Laboratory Validation, First Action 2016.12
version: Ebersole et al., AOAC Official Method 2016.12, First Action version published in 2017
locator: Official method sections A–D, apparatus and headspace/GC conditions. Sections H–J, calibration, sample preparation, peak identification and validation.
summary: The method measures ethanol with a headspace autosampler, a DB-WAXetr column and FID. It uses 1-propanol as an internal standard and identifies the peaks against reference solutions. The paper includes blank, spike and precision measurements in kombucha.
scope: The apparatus section names an Agilent 7890 GC and a Combi-PAL headspace autosampler. It gives no 7890 model suffix. A lab transferring the method needs the compatible sampler, sealed vials and the specified inlet and detector conditions.
rights: Published method hosted by Kombucha Brewers International and original catalog summary.

title: Examination of the Varied and Changing Ethanol Content of Commercial Kombucha Products
locator: Apparatus and Conditions. Table 1, external calibration and standard addition. Table 2, measured and certified reference values.
summary: The authors measured 1.12–2.00% ethanol by volume in 18 commercial kombucha samples. They checked their headspace GC-FID measurements against three NIST ethanol-water reference solutions and compared two calibration approaches.
scope: The study used a Shimadzu GC-2010 Plus with headspace autosampling, split injection and an ionic-liquid column. Its market samples and column differ from the AOAC method. Table 1 distinguishes alcohol by mass from alcohol by volume.
rights: Author's journal copy hosted by Kombucha Brewers International and original catalog summary.

title: Method for the determination of volatile compounds in virgin olive oil by SPME-GC-FID/MS
locator: Sections 1.3–1.4, instrument and SPME inlet liner. Sections 3.2.3–3.2.5 and Table 3, headspace extraction, detector options and peak identification.
summary: The method concentrates selected virgin olive oil aroma compounds on a headspace SPME fiber and desorbs them in a split/splitless inlet. It specifies FID or MS options and uses standards and retention indices to support peak identification.
scope: The calibration targets specified volatiles in an oil matrix. A headspace syringe alone does not perform solid-phase microextraction. Confirm the SPME fiber, liner and column, and use the section for the installed detector.
rights: Council method link and original catalog summary.

title: Fresh and Aromatic Virgin Olive Oil Obtained from Arbequina, Koroneiki, and Arbosana Cultivars
locator: Section 3.4, volatile measurements and calibration, p. 11. Figure 3, Arbosana response surface. Section 3.5 and Table 6, experimental design.
summary: The team measured volatile aroma compounds in oils from three olive cultivars using a headspace SPME fiber, a 7890B GC-FID, a split/splitless inlet and a DB-WAXetr column. Figure 3 shows how the total measured lipoxygenase-pathway volatiles varied with processing conditions for one cultivar.
scope: This experiment used analyte standards and an internal standard in deodorized oil. Its cultivar and processing comparisons depend on the stated preparation, fiber and calibration matrix. An FID peak alone does not identify an unknown compound.
rights: Publisher open-access article link and original catalog summary.
